case: A.K. Gopalan v. State of Madras
holding: Read 'procedure established by law' in Article 21 narrowly: a detention law only had to be validly enacted, not fair. Overruled in Maneka Gandhi (1978).

case: Romesh Thappar v. State of Madras
holding: A ban on the circulation of a journal violated Article 19(1)(a): freedom of speech includes the freedom to circulate.

case: State of Madras v. Champakam Dorairajan
holding: A communal government order allotting college seats by caste was struck down, leading to the First Amendment and Article 15(4).

case: Sankari Prasad v. Union of India
holding: The First Amendment was upheld: the power under Article 368 extends to fundamental rights, and a constitutional amendment is not 'law' under Article 13.

case: Kedar Nath Singh v. State of Bihar
holding: Sedition under Section 124A IPC was upheld but confined to words that incite violence or public disorder; strong criticism of government is not sedition.

case: Kharak Singh v. State of U.P.
holding: Domiciliary visits by police at night were struck down under Article 21; the minority view of Subba Rao J. that privacy is part of personal liberty was later adopted in Puttaswamy.

case: Sajjan Singh v. State of Rajasthan
holding: The Seventeenth Amendment was upheld, following Sankari Prasad, but two judges doubted whether fundamental rights could be amended at will, setting up Golaknath.

case: I.C. Golaknath v. State of Punjab
holding: Parliament cannot amend the Constitution so as to take away fundamental rights; applied prospectively. Overruled by Kesavananda Bharati in 1973.

case: Satwant Singh Sawhney v. D. Ramarathnam
holding: The right to travel abroad is part of personal liberty under Article 21, so a passport cannot be refused without a procedure established by law.

case: Rustom Cavasjee Cooper v. Union of India (Bank Nationalisation)
holding: Fundamental rights are not watertight compartments: a law is tested against every right it affects, and compensation for acquired property must be real, not illusory.

case: Madhav Rao Scindia v. Union of India (Privy Purses)
holding: The presidential order derecognising the rulers of former princely states to end privy purses was quashed as an abuse of power.

case: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
holding: Thirteen judges held that Parliament may amend any part of the Constitution, but cannot alter its basic structure. The widest bench in the Court's history.

case: E.P. Royappa v. State of Tamil Nadu
holding: Equality under Article 14 is a dynamic concept: arbitrariness is the antithesis of equality, so arbitrary state action is unconstitutional.

case: State of U.P. v. Raj Narain
holding: The people have a right to know every public act of their government; a claim of privilege over documents is decided by the court, not the executive.

case: Govind v. State of Madhya Pradesh
holding: Recognised a right to privacy implied in Articles 19 and 21, which must yield only to a compelling state interest.

case: Indira Nehru Gandhi v. Raj Narain
holding: Clause (4) of the Thirty-ninth Amendment, which put the Prime Minister's election beyond judicial scrutiny, was struck down: free and fair elections are part of the basic structure.

case: ADM Jabalpur v. Shivkant Shukla
holding: During the Emergency no one could move a court for habeas corpus; Khanna J. dissented alone. Overruled expressly in Puttaswamy (2017).

case: State of Rajasthan v. Balchand
holding: 'The basic rule may perhaps be tersely put as bail, not jail': Krishna Iyer J. on when an accused should be kept in custody.

case: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
holding: The procedure that deprives a person of life or liberty under Article 21 must be fair, just and reasonable; Articles 14, 19 and 21 are read together.

case: Nandini Satpathy v. P.L. Dani
holding: The right against self-incrimination in Article 20(3) extends to police questioning, and an accused may remain silent; counsel may be present.

case: Sunil Batra v. Delhi Administration
holding: Prisoners retain their fundamental rights: solitary confinement of a prisoner under sentence of death and bar fetters without judicial oversight were curtailed.

case: Hussainara Khatoon v. Home Secretary, State of Bihar
holding: A speedy trial is part of the right to life and liberty under Article 21; undertrials held longer than the maximum sentence were ordered released.

case: Prem Shankar Shukla v. Delhi Administration
holding: Routine handcuffing of prisoners is unconstitutional; restraint needs a recorded reason and judicial permission except in extreme cases.

case: Bachan Singh v. State of Punjab
holding: The death penalty is constitutional but may be imposed only in the 'rarest of rare' cases, after weighing aggravating and mitigating circumstances.

case: Ratlam Municipality v. Vardhichand
holding: A municipality cannot plead lack of funds to avoid abating a public nuisance; Section 133 CrPC (now 152 BNSS) is a tool for the citizen.

case: Minerva Mills v. Union of India
holding: Clauses (4) and (5) of Article 368 were struck down: a limited amending power is itself a basic feature, as is the balance between fundamental rights and directive principles.

case: Ajay Hasia v. Khalid Mujib Sehravardi
holding: Laid down the tests for when a body is an instrumentality of the State under Article 12: financial, functional and administrative control by government.

case: Francis Coralie Mullin v. Administrator, Union Territory of Delhi
holding: The right to life includes the right to live with human dignity and all that goes with it: adequate nutrition, clothing, shelter, and the freedom to mix with fellow human beings.

case: Air India v. Nergesh Meerza
holding: Terminating an air hostess's service on her first pregnancy was struck down as arbitrary and unreasonable under Article 14.

case: Sheela Barse v. State of Maharashtra
holding: Safeguards for women in police custody: separate lock-ups guarded by women constables, interrogation only in the presence of women police, and legal aid.

case: Mithu v. State of Punjab
holding: Section 303 IPC, which made death the only sentence for murder by a life convict, was struck down: a mandatory death penalty is arbitrary.

case: Rudul Sah v. State of Bihar
holding: The Supreme Court may award compensation under Article 32 for illegal detention; a man kept in jail fourteen years after acquittal was paid for the violation of Article 21.

case: Bandhua Mukti Morcha v. Union of India
holding: Bonded labour violates Article 21; a letter can be treated as a writ petition, and the Court may appoint commissions to find facts in public interest litigation.

case: Mohd. Ahmed Khan v. Shah Bano Begum
holding: A divorced Muslim woman unable to maintain herself may claim maintenance from her former husband under Section 125 CrPC; the judgment led to the 1986 Act.

case: Olga Tellis v. Bombay Municipal Corporation
holding: The right to livelihood is part of the right to life; pavement dwellers cannot be evicted without a hearing, though the eviction itself was upheld.

case: M.C. Mehta v. Union of India (Oleum gas leak)
holding: An enterprise engaged in a hazardous activity is absolutely liable for harm, without the exceptions of Rylands v. Fletcher; the measure of compensation depends on its size.

case: Pt. Parmanand Katara v. Union of India
holding: Every doctor, in government or private practice, must give immediate aid to an accident victim without waiting for legal formalities.

case: State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal
holding: Listed the seven categories of cases in which a High Court may quash an FIR or complaint under Section 482 CrPC (now Section 528 BNSS).

case: Subhash Kumar v. State of Bihar
holding: The right to life under Article 21 includes the right to pollution-free water and air; a citizen may seek relief under Article 32 against polluters.

case: Kihoto Hollohan v. Zachillhu
holding: The Tenth Schedule (anti-defection law) was upheld, but the Speaker's decision on disqualification is subject to judicial review.

case: Mohini Jain v. State of Karnataka
holding: Charging a capitation fee violates the right to education, which flows from the right to life under Article 21.

case: Indra Sawhney v. Union of India (Mandal)
holding: Twenty-seven per cent reservation for Other Backward Classes was upheld; the creamy layer must be excluded and reservations may not exceed fifty per cent, save in extraordinary situations.

case: Unni Krishnan v. State of Andhra Pradesh
holding: Every child has a right to free education up to fourteen years under Article 21; this became Article 21A by the Eighty-sixth Amendment in 2002.

case: Nilabati Behera v. State of Orissa
holding: Compensation for a custodial death is a public-law remedy under Articles 32 and 226, distinct from a private suit; sovereign immunity is no defence.

case: Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Association v. Union of India (Second Judges case)
holding: The opinion of the Chief Justice of India, formed with senior colleagues, has primacy in judicial appointments: the collegium system was born.

case: S.R. Bommai v. Union of India
holding: A proclamation of President's rule under Article 356 is subject to judicial review, and secularism is part of the basic structure.

case: P. Rathinam v. Union of India
holding: Held that the right to life includes a right not to live and struck down Section 309 IPC; overruled two years later in Gian Kaur.

case: R. Rajagopal v. State of Tamil Nadu
holding: The right to privacy is implicit in Article 21; the press may publish the public record, including court records, without consent, but not private matters.

case: Sarla Mudgal v. Union of India
holding: A Hindu husband who converts to Islam to marry again without dissolving his first marriage commits bigamy under Section 494 IPC.

case: Indian Medical Association v. V.P. Shantha
holding: Medical treatment for a fee is a 'service' under the Consumer Protection Act, so a patient may sue a doctor or hospital before a consumer forum.

case: Bodhisattwa Gautam v. Subhra Chakraborty
holding: Rape violates the victim's right to life under Article 21; a court may award interim compensation to the victim even during the trial.

case: State of Punjab v. Gurmit Singh
holding: The testimony of a rape survivor needs no corroboration if it inspires confidence; courts must not treat her like an accomplice, and trials should be in camera.

case: Gian Kaur v. State of Punjab
holding: The right to life does not include a right to die; Section 309 IPC was upheld, overruling P. Rathinam. The question of dignity in dying was left for later.

case: Paschim Banga Khet Mazdoor Samity v. State of West Bengal
holding: Denial of emergency treatment at government hospitals violates Article 21; the State must provide adequate facilities for emergency care.

case: Vellore Citizens' Welfare Forum v. Union of India
holding: The precautionary principle and the polluter-pays principle are part of the law of the land, as elements of sustainable development.

case: M.C. Mehta v. Kamal Nath
holding: The public trust doctrine applies in India: the State holds rivers, forests and other natural resources in trust and cannot hand them to private use.

case: D.K. Basu v. State of West Bengal
holding: Eleven binding requirements for every arrest and detention, from name tags and arrest memos to a medical examination every forty-eight hours.

case: Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan
holding: Guidelines against sexual harassment at the workplace, binding until Parliament legislated; it did so with the POSH Act in 2013.

case: Apparel Export Promotion Council v. A.K. Chopra
holding: Sexual harassment does not require physical contact; an attempt to molest a subordinate is misconduct justifying dismissal.

case: Chairman, Railway Board v. Chandrima Das
holding: A foreign national raped by railway employees was awarded compensation: the right to life under Article 21 belongs to non-citizens too.

case: Danial Latifi v. Union of India
holding: The Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Divorce) Act, 1986 was upheld by reading it to require a fair and reasonable provision for the wife's whole future, made within the iddat period.

case: Pradeep Kumar Biswas v. Indian Institute of Chemical Biology
holding: A body is 'State' under Article 12 only if government control is financially, functionally and administratively deep and pervasive; CSIR qualifies.

case: Union of India v. Association for Democratic Reforms
holding: Voters have a right to know the criminal antecedents, assets and education of candidates; the Election Commission was directed to require disclosure.

case: People's Union for Civil Liberties v. Union of India
holding: Section 33B of the Representation of the People Act, which tried to limit candidate disclosures, was struck down; the voter's right to know is part of Article 19(1)(a).

case: Zahira Habibulla Sheikh v. State of Gujarat (Best Bakery)
holding: A trial in which witnesses were intimidated and the prosecution was indifferent is no trial at all; a retrial was ordered outside Gujarat.

case: Jacob Mathew v. State of Punjab
holding: A doctor is criminally liable for negligence only on gross negligence judged by the Bolam test; a credible expert opinion is needed before prosecution.

case: Rameshwar Prasad v. Union of India
holding: The dissolution of the Bihar assembly before it first met, on the Governor's report about horse-trading, was unconstitutional.

case: M. Nagaraj v. Union of India
holding: Reservation in promotion is permissible, but the State must show quantifiable data on backwardness, inadequate representation and administrative efficiency.

case: I.R. Coelho v. State of Tamil Nadu
holding: Laws placed in the Ninth Schedule after 24 April 1973 are open to challenge if they damage the basic structure; immunity is not absolute.

case: Ashoka Kumar Thakur v. Union of India
holding: Twenty-seven per cent reservation for OBCs in central educational institutions was upheld, with the creamy layer excluded.

case: Aruna Ramachandra Shanbaug v. Union of India
holding: Passive euthanasia may be permitted, with the approval of a High Court, for a patient in a permanent vegetative state.

case: Central Board of Secondary Education v. Aditya Bandopadhyay
holding: Evaluated answer sheets are 'information' under the RTI Act, and a student may inspect them.

case: Bharat Aluminium Co. v. Kaiser Aluminium Technical Services (BALCO)
holding: Part I of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act does not apply to arbitrations seated outside India; Bhatia International was overruled prospectively.

case: Lily Thomas v. Union of India
holding: Section 8(4) of the Representation of the People Act was struck down: a legislator convicted of a listed offence is disqualified at once.

case: People's Union for Civil Liberties v. Union of India (NOTA)
holding: Voters must have a 'None of the Above' option on the voting machine; the secrecy of a negative vote is part of the freedom of expression.

case: Lalita Kumari v. Government of Uttar Pradesh
holding: Registration of an FIR is mandatory when the information discloses a cognizable offence; a preliminary enquiry is allowed only in limited categories and must finish within days.

case: Suresh Kumar Koushal v. Naz Foundation
holding: Section 377 IPC was held constitutional, reversing the Delhi High Court; overruled in Navtej Singh Johar in 2018.

case: National Legal Services Authority v. Union of India
holding: Transgender persons have the right to self-identify their gender as male, female or third gender, and are entitled to the protection of Articles 14, 15, 19 and 21.

case: Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar
holding: No automatic arrest in Section 498A cases: police must satisfy the Section 41 CrPC checklist (now Section 35 BNSS) and magistrates must record reasons before authorising detention.

case: Manoj Narula v. Union of India
holding: The Court cannot bar persons facing serious charges from the council of ministers, but the Prime Minister is expected not to appoint them, as a matter of constitutional trust.

case: Anvar P.V. v. P.K. Basheer
holding: An electronic record is admissible only with the certificate under Section 65B(4) of the Evidence Act (now Section 63 BSA); oral evidence cannot replace it.

case: Shreya Singhal v. Union of India
holding: Section 66A of the IT Act was struck down as vague and overbroad; online speech enjoys the same protection as any other under Article 19(1)(a).

case: Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Association v. Union of India (NJAC)
holding: The Ninety-ninth Amendment and the National Judicial Appointments Commission Act were struck down for undermining judicial independence; the collegium was restored.

case: Subramanian Swamy v. Union of India
holding: Criminal defamation under Sections 499 and 500 IPC (now Section 356 BNS) was upheld as a reasonable restriction protecting reputation, itself part of Article 21.

case: Nabam Rebia v. Deputy Speaker, Arunachal Pradesh
holding: A Governor cannot advance an assembly session or dictate its agenda without the aid and advice of the council of ministers.

case: Krishna Kumar Singh v. State of Bihar
holding: Re-promulgating ordinances without placing them before the legislature is a fraud on the Constitution; an ordinance must be laid before the House.

case: Abhiram Singh v. C.D. Commachen
holding: An appeal for votes in the name of the religion, race, caste, community or language of the voter or the candidate is a corrupt practice under Section 123(3) of the Representation of the People Act.

case: Shayara Bano v. Union of India
holding: Instant triple talaq (talaq-e-biddat) was set aside by a majority of three to two as manifestly arbitrary.

case: K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India
holding: Nine judges unanimously held that privacy is a fundamental right protected by Article 21 and the freedoms in Part III; ADM Jabalpur was overruled.

case: Amardeep Singh v. Harveen Kaur
holding: The six-month cooling-off period for divorce by mutual consent under Section 13B(2) of the Hindu Marriage Act is directory and may be waived by the court.

case: Independent Thought v. Union of India
holding: Sexual intercourse with a wife aged between fifteen and eighteen is rape: Exception 2 to Section 375 IPC was read down to protect child wives.

case: Nikesh Tarachand Shah v. Union of India
holding: The twin conditions for bail in Section 45 of the PMLA were struck down as arbitrary; Parliament amended the section in 2018 and it was later upheld.

case: Common Cause v. Union of India
holding: The right to die with dignity is part of Article 21: passive euthanasia and advance medical directives (living wills) are lawful, with safeguards.

case: Shakti Vahini v. Union of India
holding: Honour killings and the interference of khap panchayats with a couple's choice were condemned; preventive, remedial and punitive guidelines were issued.

case: State (NCT of Delhi) v. Union of India
holding: The Lieutenant Governor is bound by the aid and advice of the Delhi council of ministers on all matters except land, police and public order.

case: Tehseen Poonawalla v. Union of India
holding: Mob lynching was condemned as a crime against the rule of law; the Court issued preventive, remedial and punitive measures and asked Parliament to make it a separate offence.

case: Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India
holding: Section 377 IPC was read down: consensual sexual acts between adults of the same sex are not an offence.

case: Social Action Forum for Manav Adhikar v. Union of India
holding: The 'family welfare committees' created in Rajesh Sharma for Section 498A complaints were done away with; the safeguards of Arnesh Kumar remain.

case: Public Interest Foundation v. Union of India
holding: Candidates and parties must publish the criminal cases pending against a candidate; the Court declined to bar charge-sheeted persons from contesting.

case: K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India (Aadhaar)
holding: The Aadhaar Act was upheld in substance, but linking with bank accounts and mobile numbers was struck down, and Section 57 on private use was read down.

case: Jarnail Singh v. Lachhmi Narain Gupta
holding: The creamy layer principle applies to Scheduled Castes and Tribes in promotions, but the State need not collect data on their backwardness.

case: Swapnil Tripathi v. Supreme Court of India
holding: Live streaming of Supreme Court proceedings of constitutional importance was approved as part of open justice.

case: Joseph Shine v. Union of India
holding: Section 497 IPC (adultery) was struck down as treating a wife as her husband's property; adultery remains a ground for divorce.

case: Indian Young Lawyers Association v. State of Kerala (Sabarimala)
holding: The exclusion of women aged ten to fifty from the Sabarimala temple was held unconstitutional by four judges to one; review petitions referred larger questions to a nine-judge bench.

case: Nipun Saxena v. Union of India
holding: The identity of a victim of rape or of a POCSO offence may not be disclosed by anyone, including the media and the police, even after death.

case: Swiss Ribbons v. Union of India
holding: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code was upheld in full, including the distinction between financial and operational creditors.

case: National Investigation Agency v. Zahoor Ahmad Shah Watali
holding: Under Section 43D(5) of the UAPA a court considering bail looks only at whether the accusation is prima facie true on the material; it does not weigh the evidence.

case: Rupali Devi v. State of Uttar Pradesh
holding: A wife driven from the matrimonial home may file a Section 498A complaint where she takes shelter; the court there has jurisdiction.

case: Committee of Creditors of Essar Steel v. Satish Kumar Gupta
holding: The commercial wisdom of the committee of creditors on a resolution plan is not open to judicial review on merits; the 330-day limit is directory in rare cases.

case: Anuradha Bhasin v. Union of India
holding: Freedom of speech and of trade through the internet are protected by Article 19; an indefinite internet suspension is impermissible and orders must be published and reviewed.

case: Arjun Panditrao Khotkar v. Kailash Kushanrao Gorantyal
holding: The Section 65B(4) certificate is a condition precedent to admitting an electronic record, unless the device is not in the party's control; Shafhi Mohammad was overruled.

case: Vineeta Sharma v. Rakesh Sharma
holding: A daughter is a coparcener by birth under the 2005 amendment to the Hindu Succession Act, whether or not her father was alive on 9 September 2005.

case: Vidya Drolia v. Durga Trading Corporation
holding: A four-fold test for when a dispute is not arbitrable; landlord-tenant disputes under the Transfer of Property Act are arbitrable.

case: Union of India v. K.A. Najeeb
holding: Section 43D(5) of the UAPA does not bar bail where the trial has been delayed for years; Article 21 prevails over the statutory restriction.

case: Dr. Jaishri Laxmanrao Patil v. Chief Minister (Maratha reservation)
holding: The Maratha reservation was struck down: the fifty per cent ceiling of Indra Sawhney stands and no extraordinary situation justified exceeding it.

case: Neil Aurelio Nunes v. Union of India
holding: OBC reservation in the NEET all-India quota was upheld; merit cannot be reduced to marks in an open examination, and reservation is not opposed to merit.

case: Satender Kumar Antil v. Central Bureau of Investigation
holding: Guidelines on bail by category of offence: no arrest where Sections 41 and 41A CrPC are not followed, and bail applications to be decided within set time limits.

case: Vijay Madanlal Choudhary v. Union of India
holding: The main provisions of the PMLA were upheld: the twin bail conditions in Section 45, the ED's powers of arrest and search, and the ECIR not being an FIR.

case: X v. Principal Secretary, Health and Family Welfare, Government of NCT of Delhi
holding: An unmarried woman may terminate a pregnancy up to twenty-four weeks under the MTP Act and Rules; the distinction between married and unmarried women is unconstitutional.

case: Janhit Abhiyan v. Union of India
holding: The One Hundred and Third Amendment giving ten per cent reservation to economically weaker sections was upheld by three judges to two.

case: Vivek Narayan Sharma v. Union of India (Demonetisation)
holding: The 2016 demonetisation of five-hundred and thousand-rupee notes was upheld by four judges to one as within the Central Government's power under the RBI Act.

case: Kaushal Kishor v. State of Uttar Pradesh
holding: No restrictions beyond Article 19(2) can be placed on a minister's speech; the rights under Articles 19 and 21 can be enforced even against private persons.

case: Anoop Baranwal v. Union of India
holding: Until Parliament legislates, the Election Commissioners are to be appointed on the advice of a committee of the Prime Minister, the Leader of the Opposition and the Chief Justice of India.

case: Shilpa Sailesh v. Varun Sreenivasan
holding: The Supreme Court may dissolve a marriage under Article 142 on the ground of irretrievable breakdown, and may waive the cooling-off period for mutual consent divorce.

case: Government of NCT of Delhi v. Union of India (Services)
holding: The elected government of Delhi has legislative and executive power over 'services', except public order, police and land.

case: Subhash Desai v. Principal Secretary, Governor of Maharashtra
holding: The Governor's call for a floor test without objective material was not justified; the Speaker must decide disqualification petitions, and Nabam Rebia was referred to seven judges.

case: Pankaj Bansal v. Union of India
holding: The Enforcement Directorate must furnish the grounds of arrest in writing to the arrested person; oral communication is not enough.

case: Supriyo v. Union of India
holding: There is no fundamental right to marry; recognition of same-sex marriage was left to Parliament, though queer couples' right to cohabit without discrimination was affirmed.

case: Cox and Kings v. SAP India
holding: The group of companies doctrine is part of Indian arbitration law: a non-signatory may be bound by an arbitration agreement by its conduct and the parties' intention.

case: In re Article 370 of the Constitution
holding: The abrogation of Article 370 was upheld: it was a temporary provision, and the President's power to declare it inoperative survived the dissolution of the Constituent Assembly of the State.

case: In re Interplay between Arbitration Agreements and the Stamp Act
holding: Seven judges held that an unstamped or insufficiently stamped arbitration agreement is not void or unenforceable; stamping is a curable defect, and N.N. Global was overruled.

case: Association for Democratic Reforms v. Union of India (Electoral bonds)
holding: The electoral bond scheme and the amendments enabling anonymous corporate donations were struck down as violating the voter's right to information.

case: Prabir Purkayastha v. State (NCT of Delhi)
holding: The written grounds of arrest must be supplied to a person arrested under the UAPA as well; the arrest and remand of the NewsClick founder were set aside.

case: State of Punjab v. Davinder Singh
holding: Seven judges held that States may sub-classify Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes to give preference to the most backward among them; E.V. Chinnaiah was overruled.

case: Manish Sisodia v. Directorate of Enforcement
holding: Bail is the rule and jail the exception even under the PMLA; a long incarceration without the trial beginning entitles the accused to bail.
